Promoting Decent Work through Strengthening OSH Management

description.narrative:
The project goal is to promote occupational safety and health (OSH) and a well-functioning Labour Inspectorate, LI. Whereas the objectives of the intervention are: - Align Kosovo OSH legislation with EU Directives and ILO conventions - Establish Labour Inspectorate Information System, LIIS Enhance OSH management by strengthening knowledge management and capacity building. - To promote occupational safety and health (OSH) and a well-functioning labour inspectorate. - To integrate gender issues into its analyses, formulation and monitoring of policies, programmes, and preventive measures to reduce inequalities between men and women in occupational safety and health (OSH).
This contribution is in line with the with the new Strategy for Sweden's reform cooperation for the Western Balkans and Turkey for 2021-2027, and its result 1: Human Rights, Democracy, the Rule of Law and Gender Equality and result 4: Inclusive Economic Development, improved opportunities for productive employment with decent working conditions.
The contribution is in line with the SDG 8.8 - Promoting labour rights and safe working environments. Outcome 3: By 2025, women and men in Kosovo, particularly youth and vulnerable groups, have increased access to decent work and benefit from sustainable and inclusive economic development that is more resilient to impacts of climate.

Projektets mål är att främja och förbättra arbetsmiljö och säkerhet och en väl fungerande yrkesinspektion.
Projektet kommer i sin analys integrera genusfrågor, utformning och uppföljning av policyer, program och förebyggande åtgärder för att minska ojämlikhet mellan män och kvinnor i arbetssäkerhet och hälsa (OSH).
Projektet har tre huvudmål:
- Kosovos arbetsmiljölagstiftning, vilket är anpassad efter EU:s direktiv och ILO:s konventioner
- Kosovos arbetsinspektionssystem anpassat efter ILO-standarder och EU-praxis
– Arbetsmiljöarbetet stärks genom att stärka kunskapshanteringen och kapacitetsuppbyggnaden
Detta bidrag ligger i linje med den nya strategin för Sveriges reformsamarbete för västra Balkan och Turkiet för 2021–2027, och dess resultatområde Mänskliga rättigheter, demokrati, rättsstatsprincipen och jämställdhet & inkluderande ekonomisk utveckling; Förbättrade anställningar och anständiga arbetsvillkor.

The project objective is to promote occupational safety and health (OSH) and a well-functioning labour inspectorate.
The project will integrate gender issues into its analyses, formulation and monitoring of policies, programmes, and preventive measures to reduce inequalities between men and women in occupational safety and health (OSH).
The project has three main goals:
- Kosovar OSH legislation is aligned with EU Directives and ILO conventions
- Kosovar labour inspection system is aligned with relevant ILO standards and EU practices
- OSH management is enhanced by strengthening knowledge management and capacity building
This contribution is in line with the with the new Strategy for Sweden's reform cooperation for the Western Balkans and Turkey for 2021-2027, and its result area Human Rights, Democracy, the Rule of Law and Gender Equality & Inclusive economic development; Improved opportunities for productive employment with decent working conditions.

The main achievements of the "Promoting Decent Work through Strengthening OSH Management" project during the implementation period from 15 April 2022 to 31 March 2025 include concrete results in aligning the labour inspection system with relevant ILO standards and EU practices, from which we would like to highlight the following:
Labour inspection system alignment with relevant ILO standards & EU practices
The project actively advocated for legislative reforms in labour inspection and occupational safety and health (OSH) at both central and local levels. In 2022 and 2023, four meetings of the "Informal Advocacy Task Force on OSH and Decent Work" were held with UN Women's support to address key challenges and push for reforms. ILO specialists provided preliminary recommendations for amending Law No. 08/L-067 on Inspections and Law No. 04/L-161 on OSH to align with international labour standards. Although these laws were included in the governments legislative agenda annually, no significant progress was made. Despite continued advocacy, the government showed little willingness to advance the amendments, resulting in no substantial legal updates during the project period and limiting the achievement of its intended outcomes.
a. At the request of the Labour Inspectorate, the ILO provided technical support for developing the Labour Inspectorate Development Strategy 20232027. The Strategy was shaped through an inclusive consultative process, including two stakeholder workshops held on 12 October and 7 December 2022, and was formally validated on 25 February 2023. It is currently under implementation and monitoring by the Labour Inspectorate. The Strategy outlines clear objectives and practical steps to enhance the efficiency, professionalism, and impact of labour inspection services in Kosovo and is fully aligned with ILO conventions and OSH recommendations.
To build inspector capacity in line with the new Strategy, the ILO delivered two training modules in 2023. The first, held from 13 to 16 February 2023 by the ILO LABADMIN/OSH branch, focused on labour inspection in the construction sector and was attended by 14 inspectors who received certificates from the Kosovo Institute for Public Administration (KIPA). The second, held from 29 to 31 March 2023 and supported by UN Women and KIPA, focused on gender equality in OSH, enabling 24 inspectors to address gender-specific OSH risks and workplace sexual harassment. In addition, two training modules were delivered in 2023 to strengthen labour inspectors capacity. The first, held from 13 to 16 February and delivered by ILO LABADMIN/OSH, focused on construction sector safety, addressing the high rate of accidents and fatalities. Fourteen inspectors from across Kosovo participated and received KIPA-issued certificates. The second module, held from 29 to 31 March with support from UN Women and KIPA, focused on gender equality in OSH, training 24 inspectors on gender-specific risks and workplace sexual harassment.
b. Technical support to the Labour Inspectorate was extended in support of developing and piloting the Labour Inspectorate Development Strategys Electronic Case Management System (ECMS). The first phase aligned procedural workflows and developed the systems wireframe and Software Requirements Specification, supported by workshops on 45 April and 1416 June 2023. The second phase involved IT setup, software development, and an initial pilot in Ferizaj with six inspectors trained on 1213 September 2024.
To strengthen occupational safety and health (OSH) standards and promote a prevention culture in Kosovo, the ILO conducted capacity-building and engagement activities from 2022 to 2024, targeting government, workers, employers organizations, and civil society. The first key activity was a tripartite blended training on 1920 October 2022, involving 20 representatives to improve OSH understanding and implementation. In 2023, institutional capacity was further reinforced through several trainings: three public officials (two women, one man) from the Ministry of Finance, Labour, and Transfers attended an OSH program training at the ILOs International Training Centre (ITC) in Turin (1526 May); the Chief Labour Inspector completed the Academy on Labour Administration and Inspection at ITC (23 October3 November); and six NGO representatives from LENS, QPA, and IKS completed a virtual OSH course supported by Swedens Community Development Fund.
The ILO also facilitated coordination meetings between civil society, social partners, and government institutions on 8 September 2022, 1 December 2022, 31 March 2023, and 14 August 2023, enhancing cooperation on OSH and decent work. A draft report on employment injury protection, highlighting benefit gaps and policy reform options, was produced and discussed in a workshop on 28 December 2023.
Aligned with Government Policy No. 260/2020 on zero tolerance for workplace sexual harassment, UN Women led targeted trainings: in 2022 reaching 36 public HR officials, 10 women entrepreneurs, 14 university reps, 17 vocational education reps, and 5 OSH practitioners; and in 2023 reaching 200 public officials, 20 women entrepreneurs, and 16 journalists.
In 2024, the ILO, in partnership with the Labour Inspectorate and with ITC Turins support, launched an online interactive OSH course for low-risk industries on E-Kosova. The course promotes awareness and prevention among workers and employers; within three months, 181 people completed at least one module, and 102 finished all. This initiative was co-financed by the ILO Technical Cooperation budget and the ESAP II regional project.
c. The ILO-supported Decent Work for a Dignified Life OSH campaign ran from December 2022 to May 2023, raising awareness about workplace safety, especially in construction. For World Day for Safety and Health (28 April 2023), the Labour Inspectorate, with ILO support, released a video on construction accidents that reached over 200,000 viewers. UN Womens study on workplace sexual harassment informed a campaign with a TV ad, debate, and infographics to promote dialogue. Six Kosovo enterprises signed the Womens Empowerment Principles in 20222023, committing to gender equality at work.
On 26 April 2024, the Safety and Health Day Conference in Pristina gathered 80 stakeholders to discuss OSH challenges. The event was co-financed by the ESAP III project.
In conclusion, the project has achieved tangible and important results, including LIs 20232027 strategy, a revised organizational structure, digital tools like the ECMS, and extensive training and awareness campaigns. While legislative reforms are still pending, the project significantly strengthened institutional capacity and ownership in OSH policymaking, therefore, continued support to the ILO remains essential for the further development of the Labour Inspectorate.
